paper.title_en: Highly correlated exponential variational method applied to the <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> system
paper.abstract_en: Recent calculations based on the same HAL QCD Collaboration <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> lattice-QCD potential have reached conflicting conclusions on whether the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> system supports a bound state. The problem is reexamined here with a highly correlated exponential variational method. The near-threshold state is directly evaluated without coupling-constant extrapolation, and the Coulomb interaction is treated through analytically exact matrix elements. Without Coulomb, the variational energy lies below the <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> threshold, indicating a shallow <math><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mtext>–</mtext><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> bound state with a binding energy of about 0.025 MeV. The resulting bound state is spatially extended, with <math><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo>〈</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>〉</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>≈</mo><mn>17.5</mn></mrow></math> fm, consistent with the near-threshold scale <math><mrow><msup><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> fm (rms <math><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> fm). When Coulomb repulsion is included, the variational energy approaches the threshold from above while the rms separation grows strongly and remains unconverged; no binding signal is found within the explored basis sizes. Complex-scaling calculations likewise yield no <math><mi>θ</mi></math>-stable resonance pole. In the Coulomb-free model, a survey of the nine spin-channel/time-slice combinations finds only the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> case below threshold.
